# Colten Ellis

## Early Life and Junior Career

Colten Ellis is a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender who currently plays for the Buffalo Sabres in the National Hockey League (NHL) . His journey from a remote community in Nova Scotia to the professional ranks represents a significant narrative of perseverance and athletic talent, forming the foundation of his notability. Born on October 5, 2000, in River Denys, Nova Scotia, a community noted for its small population of only 60 residents, Ellis's path to elite hockey was paved with challenges unique to his geographic origin , . Despite the lack of specialized training facilities for goaltenders in his hometown, Ellis began his goaltending training at the age of ten, demonstrating an early commitment to the position . His father, Brian Ellis, stated in a 2020 interview that the process was "really, really hard," but the family made every effort to provide him with the necessary resources to improve . This familial support was crucial, as Cape Breton West Major Midget Islanders president Brian Macinnis highlighted Ellis's exceptional dedication to traveling for camps and training sessions, overcoming the significant geographic barriers inherent to his situation . This early adversity underscores the determination that would later characterize his development.

Ellis's youth hockey career began with the Cape Breton West MHA, where he honed his skills before moving up to the major midget level . His success at this stage culminated in a historic achievement in 2017 when he backstopped the Cape Breton West Islanders to a gold medal victory at the TELUS Cup, the national midget hockey championship , . This triumph was particularly significant as it marked the first time a team from Atlantic Canada had won the prestigious tournament . In the gold medal game held in Prince George, British Columbia, Ellis delivered a standout performance, making 43 saves, including 22 in the third period and a critical breakaway save in overtime, to secure the victory . He remains in contact with many of his former teammates from this successful team . This early success established him as a player capable of leading his team to the highest levels of junior competition and demonstrated his ability to perform under immense pressure. His connection to his roots remains strong; he credits his recovery from a season-ending hip surgery in February 2023 with renewing his love for the game and credits veteran goaltender Malcolm Subban for mentoring him during his transition from the ECHL to the American Hockey League (AHL) .

His professional aspirations took a significant step forward on March 1, 2021, when he signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the St. Louis Blues , . This signing was a landmark moment for his home region, as he became the first goaltender from Cape Breton Island to sign an NHL contract, a fact confirmed by the CEO of the Nova Scotia Sports Hall of Fame . This achievement solidified his status as a trailblazer for aspiring athletes from his community. Before embarking on his professional career, Ellis completed a robust junior hockey career within the Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League (QMJHL), playing for multiple franchises including the Charlottetown Islanders, Rimouski Océanic, and the Cape Breton West Islanders , . Over his career in the league, he played 153 games, compiling an impressive record of 103 wins, 31 losses, and 4 ties, along with 18 shutouts . During this time, he also posted a respectable 2.31 goals-against average (GAA) and a .912 save percentage . His performance earned him numerous accolades and recognition as one of the top goaltenders in the league.

The pinnacle of Ellis's junior career came during the 2020–21 season with the Charlottetown Islanders, a campaign that saw him achieve unprecedented statistical success and set multiple records . He led the entire QMJHL in several key goaltending categories, earning the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy as the league’s best goaltender , . That same season, he also claimed the Raymond Lagacé Trophy as the league’s Defensive Rookie of the Year . His dominance was most evident in his single-season statistics, where he set the QMJHL record for the lowest goals-against average at 1.78 , . He also tied the single-season shutout record with seven shutouts, a mark previously shared by notable goalies like Roberto Luongo , . Furthermore, his .926 save percentage ranked as the fourth-best single-season mark in league history, showcasing his ability to consistently make difficult saves , . On March 22, 2021, in a 4–0 win over the Cape Breton Eagles, Ellis broke the all-time QMJHL career shutout record, recording his 18th career shutout , . Reflecting on the milestone, he noted that it was not something he had actively pursued, but its significance was amplified by the presence of his family and friends in attendance . This remarkable body of work in the QMJHL firmly established him as one of the premier prospects in North American junior hockey and laid the groundwork for his selection in the 2019 NHL Entry Draft.

## Professional Development with the St. Louis Blues

Following his record-setting junior career, Colten Ellis was selected by the St. Louis Blues in the third round of the 2019 NHL Entry Draft, chosen 93rd overall , . At the time of the draft, he was highly regarded as one of the top goaltender prospects available from the QMJHL . Scouting reports provided a nuanced analysis of his skill set. Corey Pronman of The Athletic described him as "one of the most athletic goalies available," praising his powerful legs, quick push-offs, and strong anticipation . However, he also noted areas for improvement, including "extra movement" and inconsistent puck tracking, alongside concerns about his 6'1" frame . Similarly, Bill Placzek characterized him as technically sound and calm, with excellent flexibility and smooth control, but flagged rebound control and behind-the-puck handling as developmental needs . These assessments paint a picture of a talented athlete with a high ceiling but still possessing elements of his game that required refinement at the professional level. Prior to his draft, Ellis had also attended Team Canada’s 2020 World Juniors development camp, indicating his status as a recognized national prospect .

After signing his entry-level contract with the Blues, Ellis embarked on the typical developmental path through their farm system . He began his professional career in the East Coast Hockey League (ECHL), playing for the Orlando Solar Bears, before progressing to their primary American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate, the Springfield Thunderbirds , . This progression showcased his steady advancement and ability to compete at higher levels of professional hockey. During his tenure with the Thunderbirds, he quickly established himself as a reliable starting goaltender. In the 2023–24 season, he posted an outstanding 22–14–2 record with a 2.62 GAA and a .922 save percentage, demonstrating his capacity to handle a heavy workload and maintain a high level of performance . His consistent play earned him significant praise from Blues management; General Manager Doug Armstrong and head coach Jim Montgomery both lauded him, with Armstrong calling him a "premier goalie in the American League" and Montgomery describing him as "a guy you cheer for" due to his work ethic and positive development trajectory . His leadership and impact on the team were further recognized when he was named the Team MVP by the Springfield Thunderbirds .

Despite his success in the AHL, Ellis remained part of a crowded goaltending depth chart in the St. Louis organization. As the projected No. 3 NHL goaltender, he was slated to continue developing with the Thunderbirds, serving as the backup to established NHL veterans Jordan Binnington and Joel Hofer . His status as a waiver-exempt player changed as he aged and progressed through his contract, making him eligible to be claimed by another team . Throughout his three seasons in the AHL, he compiled a cumulative record of 27–19–8 in 53 games, while his time across three ECHL seasons resulted in a 39–27–11 record in 82 games, highlighting his experience and consistency in the minor leagues . He also represented his country internationally, being named to Team Canada's roster for the 2024 Spengler Cup, an invitational tournament in Davos, Switzerland . His selection was notable as he became the first active player from the Springfield Thunderbirds to participate in the event, which is recognized as the world's oldest international club invitational tournament . Through 31 appearances in the 2024–25 season with the Thunderbirds prior to his waiver claim, he maintained a solid 19–7–3 record with a .926 save percentage and a 2.41 goals-against average, cementing his value as a top-tier minor league goaltender . This period of development within the Blues organization served as the essential proving ground that prepared him for the opportunity that awaited him in Buffalo.

## Acquisition by the Buffalo Sabres and NHL Debut

The pivotal turning point in Colten Ellis's professional career occurred on October 6, 2024, when he was claimed off waivers by the Buffalo Sabres from the St. Louis Blues , . Several sources confirm the timing of this move around late October 2024, with some citing October 7 or even October 16, likely reflecting different reporting timelines surrounding the same transaction , . This waiver claim was a strategic move by the Sabres, who were navigating a challenging start to the 2024–25 season. The team was dealing with roster adjustments, including placing starting goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen on injured reserve with a lower-body injury, which created an immediate need in net . With the regular starter, Alexandar Georgiev, also underperforming, the Sabres saw an opportunity to acquire a proven, young goaltender to stabilize their crease . For Ellis, being claimed off waivers was the long-awaited chance to finally enter the National Hockey League, having spent four seasons developing within the Blues' system without an NHL appearance , .

The Sabres acted swiftly to integrate Ellis into their lineup. Just one day after claiming him, on October 7, 2024, they named him to their opening-night roster for the 2024–25 NHL season, marking his first-ever inclusion on an NHL opening-night roster . This decision signaled the team's confidence in his abilities and their intention to utilize him as a starting goaltender. Originally, Ellis was slated to begin the season with the Springfield Thunderbirds, the Blues' AHL affiliate, but the waiver claim elevated him directly to the NHL level . He was scheduled to make his potential debut as the Sabres' starting goaltender in their home game against the Colorado Avalanche on October 14, 2024, but that game was postponed . His official debut would come several weeks later, but the stage was set for his arrival in the league. The move was widely seen as a low-risk, high-reward acquisition for Buffalo, giving them a fresh arm with a strong track record in the AHL . Ellis himself resided in Buffalo, New York, by this time, suggesting he was already in the area and ready to step in should an opportunity arise .

Colten Ellis made his highly anticipated NHL debut on Wednesday night, December 11, 2024, in a game against the Detroit Red Wings at KeyBank Center in Buffalo , . The game held special significance beyond the on-ice result; Ellis stopped 27 of 29 shots to secure a 4–2 victory, becoming the first goaltender born in Cape Breton to play and earn a win in an NHL game , . This achievement added another layer of historical context to his story, reinforcing his role as a pioneer from his small hometown . He also joined an exclusive group of Sabres goaltenders, becoming the ninth player in franchise history to record a win in his NHL debut , . His performance was particularly noteworthy for his composure and ability to make crucial saves. He stood tall against two dangerous breakaways—one by Marco Kasper late in the first period and another by Dylan Larkin early in the second period—demonstrating the mental toughness required at the highest level of the sport , . The Associated Press, providing independent coverage, highlighted these key moments, contextualizing his debut with his biographical significance and the narrative of his journey from River Denys . His debut was a textbook example of a successful transition from the minors to the majors, validating the Sabres' decision to claim him and setting a positive tone for his rookie season. Jack Quinn contributed significantly to the win with a goal and two assists, but the spotlight was firmly on the new Sabres goaltender who had just etched his name into the team's history books .

## Early Career with the Buffalo Sabres

Following the successful storybook debut, Colten Ellis continued to build upon his promising start with the Buffalo Sabres during the 2025–26 NHL season. His initial four starts were particularly impressive, as he compiled a 3–1 record and posted a .914 save percentage, winning three of those decisions , . This strong performance drew positive attention from media outlets, with ESPN rating the struggling Sabres 27th out of 32 NHL teams in its power rankings but identifying Ellis as a "bright spot amid an otherwise difficult season" . The publication went on to describe him as a "potential hidden gem," a label that suggests a belief in his long-term value and potential to become a cornerstone of the team's goaltending corps . This external validation was matched by internal organizational confidence. Sabres management reportedly instructed Ellis to look for a long-term residence in Buffalo, a clear indication that they viewed him not as a temporary fix but as a player integral to their future plans .

His early success included back-to-back wins in mid-December 2025. On Saturday, December 13, he started and won a 5–4 overtime game against the Edmonton Oilers, stopping 32 of 35 shots and earning second-star honors for his performance . Then, on Monday, December 15, he secured another victory, this time in a 5–1 win over the Detroit Red Wings, making 24 saves on 28 shots . These consecutive wins solidified his standing as the Sabres' primary goaltender and demonstrated his ability to carry the team to victory. Over his first five NHL games, from November 17 to December 9, 2025, he recorded three wins (including one in overtime and one in a shootout), one loss, and one loss in regulation, with his save percentages ranging from .829 to a perfect 1.000 across 242 minutes of ice time . This period showcased a combination of resilience, clutch performances, and a consistent ability to challenge opposing offenses.

However, Ellis's promising run was interrupted by a significant setback. On Tuesday, November 19, 2024, during an NHL regular-season game against the Edmonton Oilers, he appeared in net but was removed late in the first period due to an upper-body injury . This injury ended his participation in that game, and the Sabres ultimately lost the contest 4–3 in overtime . Another injury occurred on December 10, 2025, when he was again forced to exit an NHL game against the Edmonton Oilers late in the first period due to an upper-body injury, ending his participation in that match . These incidents introduced an element of uncertainty regarding his durability and raised questions about how he would manage the physical demands of an NHL season. The injury timeline appears to contain a discrepancy, with one source placing the first injury in November 2024 and another in December 2025, but the nature of the incident is consistent across reports. Despite these setbacks, he returned to the lineup and faced the Calgary Flames on December 16, 2025 , . In that game, the Sabres suffered a 6–2 loss, and Ellis suffered his first career NHL loss, having stopped 29 of 35 shots faced . This loss served as a reminder of the challenges and inconsistencies that define a professional athlete's career. After a strong start, his overall save percentage dipped to .896 following the defeat, illustrating the rollercoaster nature of goaltending at the NHL level .

## Analytical Profile and Career Statistics

Colten Ellis's career trajectory provides a compelling case study in the development of a modern-day professional goaltender. From his origins in the small community of River Denys, Nova Scotia, to his emergence as a starting-caliber NHL goaltender for the Buffalo Sabres, his path is defined by resilience, athletic talent, and a consistent work ethic , . His physical profile includes a height of 6 feet 1 inch (185 cm) and a weight reported between 185 lbs and 191 lbs across various sources, with one source noting 190 lbs , , . He catches left-handed and wears jersey number 92 for the Sabres . Beyond his immediate family, which includes a brother named Matthew and a cousin named Chase, very little personal information is available in the provided sources . His career is governed by his agency, 'Premium' . A key aspect of his professional identity is his representation by the Buffalo Sabres, whose rights he holds exclusively . His contract year was listed as 2026/27, indicating a multi-year commitment from the organization . More recently, on December 16, 2025, he signed a two-year, two-way contract extension with the team, further solidifying his future with the franchise .

An analytical look at his career reveals a player whose strengths lie in his athleticism and composure. Scouts who evaluated him before the 2019 NHL Draft praised his "powerful legs" and "quick push offs," highlighting his dynamic movements in the crease . His ability to remain calm and collected under pressure was another frequently cited attribute . Sabres head coach Lindy Ruff echoed these sentiments, emphasizing Ellis's situational awareness and "excellent" breakout decisions, which are critical skills for a modern goaltender expected to initiate plays . Coaches and teammates also commend his mental approach and discipline, noting his routine and willingness to stay late at the rink ("rink rat") to take extra shots, benefiting both himself and his teammates . However, his development has also been focused on addressing known weaknesses. Scouting reports from his pre-draft days pointed to areas needing improvement, such as rebound control and behind-the-puck handling, which are common developmental hurdles for young goalies . His own reflections after recovering from hip surgery indicate a maturation of his mindset, shifting his focus from worrying about his appearance to simply concentrating on stopping the puck, a testament to his mental toughness .

While his journey has been punctuated by the inevitable challenges of a professional sports career, including injuries, his foundational skills, mental fortitude, and the support of his organization have positioned him as a promising young talent in the NHL. His story continues to unfold, but his past accomplishments provide a solid basis for his future in professional hockey.

4.content:
Buffalo Sabres general manager Kevyn Adams has [made his fair share of mistakes](https://sabrenoise.com/7-worst-moves-by-kevyn-adams-as-buffalo-sabres-general-manager-01k0vjj51pz4) across six seasons leading the franchise's front office, but claiming goalie Colten Ellis off waivers from the St. Louis Blues just before the start of the 2025-26 campaign [looks like a hit](https://sabrenoise.com/sabres-colten-ellis-took-awesome-rookie-lap-then-proved-he-belongs-in-the-nhl-01k88gt3trv2).

Ellis, 25, compiled a .914 save percentage across his first four NHL starts, [three of which resulted in Buffalo wins](https://sabrenoise.com/colten-ellis-was-the-unsung-hero-of-the-buffalo-sabres-comeback-against-the-red-wings-01ka75v4kp5t), before a dreadful team-wide performance in a 6-2 loss to the Calgary Flames caused his overall numbers to dip considerably (.896 SV%).

[ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/47110163/nhl-power-rankings-2025-26-best-teams-standings-best-stats-projections-pace) called the 2019 third-round draft pick a "bright spot amid an otherwise difficult season" in its latest NHL power rankings, which rated the Sabres 27th out of the league's 32 teams.

"Buffalo found a potential hidden gem in goaltender Colten Ellis," ESPN wrote. "The Sabres claimed Ellis off waivers from St. Louis in October, and he has stepped in recently to help stabilize Buffalo in net."

Ellis strong play is one of the reasons the Blue and Gold have [continued to carry three netminders](https://sabrenoise.com/does-buffalo-sabres-ukko-pekka-luukkonen-have-any-nhl-trade-value-01k8jx8mze0c) on their active roster, which is a logjam Adams should [attempt to solve as quickly as possible](https://sabrenoise.com/nhl-rumors-buffalo-sabres-star-requested-trade-amid-goalie-logjam-01k8ty0h19h6).

Colten Ellis making a strong initial case to become part of the Buffalo Sabres' goaltending future
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Sabres would surely prefer to send Ellis to the AHL's Rochester Americans, where he could split starts with prized prospect Devon Levi, while trying to trade either Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen or Alex Lyon before the 2026 NHL trade deadline in March.

Given how well Ellis has played, however, it's unlikely the 6-foot-1 Canadian goalie would make it through waivers. There was [speculation earlier the campaign](https://sabrenoise.com/nhl-rumors-buffalo-sabres-fear-retribution-from-the-st-louis-blues-01k8bcbzxqxb) the Blues would claim him back if the Sabres put him on the waiver wire.

It's not just his performance at the NHL level that lends credence to the idea he's trending toward becoming at least a dependable backup. He compiled a strong .919 SV% across 64 games for the Springfield Thunderbirds, the Blues' AHL affiliate, over the past three years.

For a franchise like Buffalo, which has cycled through numerous goalies since the Ryan Miller era ended in 2014, giving up on a high-upside option like Ellis would come with plenty of risk.

It puts a lot of pressure on Adams to make the right call on how to handle the goaltending logjam.

Trading Luukkonen, who's compiled an unsightly .887 SV% in 62 outing since the beginning of last season, is the best option. Trying to [find a taker for a goalie with those numbers](https://sabrenoise.com/nhl-insider-with-surprising-update-on-ukko-pekka-luukkonen-that-buffalo-sabres-fans-won-t-like-01kb3ncyj7hy) who's signed through 2028-29 with a $4.75 million salary-cap hit won't be easy, though.

If they did, it would create a scenario where the Sabres could see what they have in Ellis and Lyon for the remainder of the current campaign and, if Ellis' standout play continues, they could potentially move forward with Ellis and Levi as their tandem.

Dealing Lyon, who was Buffalo's [best player by far in the season's early stages](https://sabrenoise.com/sorry-upl-alex-lyon-is-the-buffalo-sabres-starting-goalie-now-01k80qhx65fx), is also an option, though having UPL on the roster would still complicate matters in the years ahead.

Regardless of the direction the Sabres decide to go, it's become clear (if it wasn't already) that trying to juggle three netminders isn't a favorable environment for any of them over the long haul.

Meanwhile, Ellis should receive ample opportunities over the next few years, whether in Buffalo or elsewhere, to prove whether he's indeed capable of being a full-time NHL goalie.

His first handful of games have clearly raised his stock from a league-wide perspective.

> coughmecoughbefore he started dominating the AHL). He's not the puckhandler that Binnington and Hofer are; that's probably his biggest weakness, but otherwise, he's been rock-solid.

I have to ask, respectfully, if he was the blue's best goaltending prospect, then why on earth did Armstrong take the risk by putting him on waivers? I assume it's roster space and cap compliance related. This is the sort of move that i would be raking kevyn adams over the coals if he made a similar misstep.

Took him some time to even get an opportunity and he squandered it the first time, but took over the starting role in Springfield when Zherenko was struggling hard. I'll be keeping an eye on him in Buffalo, but he's done nothing but put up great numbers behind a team that has been rather weak on the backend and gives up a lot of shots in the AHL.

Also, \*knock on wood\* our goalies have been fortunate and have rarely gotten hurt.

As a Blues fan, I don’t like this. But as an Ellis fan, I can’t help but be happy he’s going to get a legit NHL shot now. He wasn’t going to get that soon in STL with Binnington and Hofer there.

Ellis was Springfield’s Team MVP last season and very deservedly so. The T-birds gave up the most shots against in the AHL and he was fantastic. Kept them in a lot of games they shouldn’t have been in. He pretty much never lets in a weak one. At least at the AHL level. Zero NHL experience so was figuring he would pass through waivers.

Here’s to hoping UPL is healthy soon, you guys put Ellis back on waivers and we can have him back. ![Image 6: 😉](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@14.0.2/assets/72x72/1f609.png) He has NHL potential for sure.

> Gorgiev is making a league minimum salary if he gets waived and clears, he will cost the team nothing on the cap as his entire salary will be absorbed by the AHL send down

  

> Georgiev has looked bad. I’m glad they are being proactive about the situation regardless of how recently he was signed.

Don’t get me wrong—I’m not critical of it as a move that is low risk and is good for the team. But it’s a bad look on management and pro scouting to do it. I wonder if they plan to try Ellis out in the NHL, or if they plan to call up Levi and let Ellis start in Rochester.

Regarding burying the contract: we all know this team has an internal spending cap, so while it doesn’t affect the Sabres NHL cap to bury a contract in the minors, I can’t imagine it makes the frackface in charge happy. It’s not nothing. It seems like we can’t have new assistant coaches in Buffalo over similar amounts of money. Along with any other number of resources that could improve the team if he’d spend money.

I just want to believe this reflects poorly on Adams from ownership’s vantage.

Ellis can't go to Rochester without passing waivers, and if they place him on waivers St Louis can claim him back and assign him to the AHL directly if they are the only team to put in a claim. So either someone else gets Ellis, the Blues are the only team to want him so they claim him and get to send him down, or nobody claims him but the Blues are afraid someone might (forcing them to keep him in the NHL) so they pass and then the Sabres get to send him to Rochester. Which feels unlikely.

**Colten Ellis** (born October 5, 2000) is a Canadian professional [ice hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_hockey "Ice hockey") player who is a [goaltender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goaltender "Goaltender") for the [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Sabres "Buffalo Sabres") of the [National Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hockey_League "National Hockey League") (NHL). He was selected 93rd overall by the [St. Louis Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Blues "St. Louis Blues") in the third round of the [2019 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NHL_entry_draft "2019 NHL entry draft").

Born and raised in [River Denys, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Denys,_Nova_Scotia "River Denys, Nova Scotia"), Ellis emerged as one of Atlantic Canada's top young goaltenders while playing for the Cape Breton West Islanders, leading the team and province to its first-ever [Telus Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telus_Cup "Telus Cup") in 2017. Following his performances with the Islanders, he went on to play major junior hockey in the [Quebec Major Junior Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_Major_Junior_Hockey_League "Quebec Major Junior Hockey League") (QMJHL) with the [Cape Breton Screaming Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Screaming_Eagles "Cape Breton Screaming Eagles"), the [Rimouski Océanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimouski_Oc%C3%A9anic "Rimouski Océanic"), and the [Charlottetown Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlottetown_Islanders "Charlottetown Islanders"). During his time in the QMJHL, Ellis made a name for himself, earning defensive rookie of the year and a spot on the all-rookie team his first year. Described as an athletic goalie before the 2019 NHL entry draft, he was selected by the St. Louis Blues with the 93rd overall pick. In his final QMJHL season, he tied the career QMJHL shutout record, broke the best goals-against-average season record, and had the fourth-best season save percentage all time. He was also named the best goaltender of the year and earned a spot on the first all-star team.

After signing an entry-level contract with St. Louis in 2021, Ellis spent several seasons developing within the organization. He began his professional career with the [ECHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHL "ECHL")'s [Worcester Railers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_Railers "Worcester Railers") before earning opportunities with the [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") (AHL) [Springfield Thunderbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Thunderbirds "Springfield Thunderbirds"). Following subpar performance marked by inconsistent play and a mid-season injury that sidelined him for the rest of the 2022–23 season with the ECHL [Tulsa Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Oilers "Tulsa Oilers"), Ellis rebounded after relearning his love for hockey. In the following seasons, his statistics and play improved, eventually earning the Thunderbirds' starting role. In October 2025, the Blues placed Ellis on waivers, where he was claimed by the Buffalo Sabres. He made his NHL debut later that month, becoming the first goaltender from [Cape Breton Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Island "Cape Breton Island") to play in the NHL. Internationally, he has represented the [Canada national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_men%27s_national_ice_hockey_team "Canada men's national ice hockey team").

Ellis was born in [River Denys, Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Denys,_Nova_Scotia "River Denys, Nova Scotia") on October 5, 2000, to Jo-Ann and Brian Ellis as one of three children in the family.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) He began playing hockey with the [Whycocomagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whycocomagh "Whycocomagh") Minor Hockey Association,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Whycocomagh-3) and had trouble throughout his childhood finding consistent playing time and competition, which his father helped him out with.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-4) Ellis has one brother, Matt, and one cousin, Chase, who played in the QMJHL with him.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Rimouski-5)

Ellis joined the Nova Junior X-Men of the Nova Scotia Under-15 Major Hockey League in the 2013–14 season as his first step into amateur hockey and stayed for 2014–15, having a 2.08 [goals against average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goals_against_average "Goals against average") (GAA) and a 1.61 GAA respectively.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Following the two seasons with the X-Men, he joined the Cape Breton West Islanders of the Nova Scotia Under-18 Major Hockey League for the 2015–16 season, putting up a .890 save percentage and a 3.70 GAA.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)

Following his performance with the Islanders, the [Cape Breton Screaming Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Screaming_Eagles "Cape Breton Screaming Eagles") selected Ellis in the fourth round of the 2016 [Quebec Major Junior Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_Major_Junior_Hockey_League "Quebec Major Junior Hockey League") (QMJHL) entry draft with the 59th overall pick. This was considered a noticeable drop from his expected draft position, with Screaming Eagles scouts surprised that he was still available to pick in the fourth round.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-trade-6) He attended the Screaming Eagles training camp but was assigned back to the Islanders.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Rimouski-5) Ellis brought the Islanders to winning the provincial championship, and they were entered into the Atlantic Region [Telus Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telus_Cup "Telus Cup") qualifier. They beat out the Moncton Flyers to earn themselves a spot in the Telus Cup, where they went on to become the first Nova Scotia team to win the Telus Cup.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-SO-7) Ellis performed exceptionally well in the finals and overall, with 43 saves and an overtime breakaway in the final game, along with having a 2.20 GAA and a .929 save percentage in the tournament.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Whycocomagh-3) Ellis was also called up to the Screaming Eagles throughout the [2016–17 QMJHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_QMJHL_season "2016–17 QMJHL season"), playing three games with a 2–0–0 record, a 2.50 GAA, and an .885 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-trade-6) After the end of the 2016–17 season, the Screaming Eagles decided to trade one of their three goaltenders, putting them all on the trade block. On June 3, 2017, Ellis was traded to the [Rimouski Océanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rimouski_Oc%C3%A9anic "Rimouski Océanic") for a first-round pick in the 2018 QMJHL entry draft, opting to keep their goaltenders Kyle Jessiman and [Kevin Mandolese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Mandolese "Kevin Mandolese").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-trade-6)

Ellis began the [2017–18 QMJHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_QMJHL_season "2017–18 QMJHL season") in Rimouski along with goaltender Jimmy Lemay. At the time, Rimouski general manager and head coach Serge Beausoleil did not decide on who would be starting in net for the season, as he wanted to watch and see how they develop in net.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-8) Ellis quickly took over the starting role, playing 51 games and leading the Océanic to the QMJHL playoffs. In the QMJHL playoffs, they faced the [Moncton Wildcats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncton_Wildcats "Moncton Wildcats") in the first round, which they lost in seven games.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) He ended his rookie season in the QMJHL first in wins with 33 and in shutouts with 6. He was also third in goals against average and save percentage, with 2.35 GAA and .913%, respectively.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-9) He was nominated for the [RDS Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RDS_Cup "RDS Cup"); the QMJHL rookie of the year, and the [Raymond Lagacé Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Lagac%C3%A9_Trophy "Raymond Lagacé Trophy"); the defensive rookie of the year. Teammate [Alexis Lafrenière](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Lafreni%C3%A8re "Alexis Lafrenière") won the RDS Cup while Ellis won the Raymond Lagacé Trophy. He was also named to the All-Rookie team and the second All-Star team.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-Rimouski-5)

Rimouski continued to have Ellis as the starting goaltender beginning the [2018–19 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_QMJHL_season "2018–19 QMJHL season"). Ellis was one of 40 players selected for the 2019 [CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CHL/NHL_Top_Prospects_Game "CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game"), intended as a showcase for the 2019 eligible draftees.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-10) He played just under 30 minutes in net, saving 15 out of 17 shots on goal.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-11) By the end of the season, Ellis was ranked eighth across all North American goaltenders for the [2019 NHL entry draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NHL_entry_draft "2019 NHL entry draft").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-12) In 46 games, he would record a 2.47 GAA and a .910 save percentage. Rimouski entered the 2019 playoffs as the third seed in the eastern conference, beating out the [Chicoutimi Saguenéens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicoutimi_Saguen%C3%A9ens "Chicoutimi Saguenéens") and the Screaming Eagles before being swept by the [Rouyn-Noranda Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rouyn-Noranda_Huskies "Rouyn-Noranda Huskies") in the semi-finals; Ellis had played 12 games with a 2.36 GAA and .919 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Among the media during draft talk, he was described as a very "athletic goalie" but was "moving too much" and "not tracking pucks as well as he could."[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-13) The [St. Louis Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_Blues "St. Louis Blues") selected Ellis in the third round with the 93rd overall pick in the 2019 NHL entry draft.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-14)

Ellis was returned to Rimouski for the [2019–20 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_QMJHL_season "2019–20 QMJHL season") after being drafted.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-15) He played in September and October before sustaining an injury that required surgery, which prevented him from playing in November and December.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-16) At the time of his injury, he had played 14 games with a 2.61 GAA and a .905 save percentage.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-17) On March 12, the QMJHL season was suspended for a week due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") and was [cancelled for the rest of the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_ice_hockey "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on ice hockey") on March 18.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-18) Ellis had played 29 games with a 2.41 GAA and a .904 save percentage when the season ended.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Following the end of the 2019–20 season, the [Charlottetown Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlottetown_Islanders "Charlottetown Islanders") traded for Ellis, giving up a 2020 third-round pick, and a 2021 first- and second-round pick.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-19)

Despite the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic causing the 2020–21 season for the [Ontario Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontario_Hockey_League "Ontario Hockey League") to be cancelled and the [Western Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Hockey_League "Western Hockey League") to start delayed, the [2020–21 QMJHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_QMJHL_season "2020–21 QMJHL season") continued as normal. Ellis started the season with a spot on the Week 3 QMJHL Team of the Week on October 19, recording a shutout against the [Halifax Mooseheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_Mooseheads "Halifax Mooseheads").[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-20) On March 1, 2021, Ellis signed his three-year, entry-level contract with the Blues, beginning in the [2021–22 NHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NHL_season "2021–22 NHL season").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-21) On March 22, Ellis set the all-time QMJHL record for shutouts by a goaltender with eighteen by shutting out his former team, the Screaming Eagles, 4–0.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-SO-7) He was also named Player of the Week the same day, after recording two shutouts that week.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-22) By the end of the season, he had seven shutouts, tying the single-season shutout record at the time with seven, held by six goalies, including [Hockey Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_Hall_of_Fame "Hockey Hall of Fame") inductee [Roberto Luongo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Luongo "Roberto Luongo").[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) With a record of 23–1–0 with a 1.78 GAA and .926 save percentage, Ellis set the lowest GAA for a season by a goaltender in the QMJHL, and the fourth-best all-time save percentage. For his performance in the regular season, he received the [Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Plante_Memorial_Trophy "Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy") for best goaltender and a spot on the First All-Star team.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-2021Awards-24) Ellis led the Islanders to the semi-finals of the playoffs against the [Victoriaville Tigres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoriaville_Tigres "Victoriaville Tigres"), where they lost the series 2–3.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-25)

By the [2021–22 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_ECHL_season "2021–22 ECHL season"), Ellis had aged out of the QMJHL and began his professional career, participating in the Blues' preseason training camp. After what was described as a "strong showing", he was assigned to the [Worcester Railers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester_Railers "Worcester Railers") in the [ECHL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECHL "ECHL").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-26) He made his professional debut on October 23 against the [Maine Mariners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Mariners_/(ECHL/) "Maine Mariners (ECHL)") in a 4–3 win, saving 42 out of 45 shots on goal.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-27) A week later on October 30, he was called up to the [American Hockey League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Hockey_League "American Hockey League") (AHL) [Springfield Thunderbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springfield_Thunderbirds "Springfield Thunderbirds").[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-28) He made his AHL debut against the [Bridgeport Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport_Islanders "Bridgeport Islanders"), saving 28 out of 29 shots on goal in a 4–1 win.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-29) He was sent down the next day back to the Railers. On December 9, Ellis was called up again to the Thunderbirds, staying with them for almost two months.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-30) He was sent down to the Railers for the final time on January 22.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-31) In six games on the season with the Thunderbirds, he had recorded a 1–3–2 record, a 3.93 GAA, and a .880 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) On March 18, Ellis recorded his first professional shutout against the [South Carolina Stingrays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Stingrays "South Carolina Stingrays") in a 3–0 win, making 23 saves.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-32) By the end of the season, he played 34 games with the Railers with a 15–13–5 record, a 3.21 GAA, and a .905 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)

Entering the [2022–23 ECHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_ECHL_season "2022–23 ECHL season"), Ellis participated in the Blues' Traverse City prospect tournament. He did not perform well, giving up nine goals in two starts, being pulled early both times.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-33) Ellis, along with [Joel Hofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Hofer "Joel Hofer") and Vadim Zherenko, made the Thunderbirds opening roster.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-34) Despite being on the season-opening roster, Ellis never played a game and was assigned to the ECHL [Tulsa Oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulsa_Oilers "Tulsa Oilers") on October 29.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-35) Ellis took over the Oilers starting goaltender following his reassignment. With the Oilers, he started suffering issues with his hip beginning in December and had season-ending hip surgery in February. At the time of surgery, he had finished the season with a 12–9–5 record, 3.46 GAA, and an .888 save percentage in 27 games.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-PNI-36) Ellis began his recovery period and was back on the ice in June. While recovering from his injury, Ellis had relearned his love of hockey and "re-modelled \[his\] game and took a look at what \[he\] needed to do to have some success".[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-PNI-36)

Prior to the [2023–24 ECHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_ECHL_season "2023–24 ECHL season"), Ellis participated in the Blues' training camp, where he suffered a concussion.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) He ended up being assigned to the [Orlando Solar Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Solar_Bears "Orlando Solar Bears") to start the season. Following an impressive performance with a record of 5–0–0 with one shutout, a 1.58 GAA, and a .954 save percentage, Ellis was named ECHL Goaltender of the Month for December. He was also named ECHL Goaltender of the Week ending December 23 with 2 wins, a 1.00 GAA, and a .973 save percentage.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-37) After Thunderbirds goalie Vadim Zherenko suffered an injury in January, Ellis was called up to the Thunderbirds on the 21st, playing 13 games and recording a 2.86 GAA and a .926 save percentage while Zherenko was out. Following Zherenko's return from injury, the Thunderbirds rotated him, Zherenko, and [Malcolm Subban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Subban "Malcolm Subban") in net before Subban was traded in March to the [Columbus Blue Jackets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus_Blue_Jackets "Columbus Blue Jackets").[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) Following the trade, Zherenko and Ellis became the Thunderbirds goaltender tandem and were in net for the rest of the season, playing three more games for a season total 2.89 GAA and .924 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Ellis credited Subban for his better performance in Springfield throughout the year.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TP-23) On June 11, Ellis signed a one-year, two-way contract extension worth $775,000 with the Blues.[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-38)

Ellis started the 2024–25 season by participating again in the Blues' training camp, where he would be assigned to the Thunderbirds to start the season.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-39) Despite Zherenko starting in the Thunderbirds net on opening night, he quickly took over as the team's starting goaltender, playing 8 out of the 12 games from the start of the season to mid-November with a .919 save percentage and a 2.80 GAA between that time period.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-40) Following his strong start to the AHL season, he continued to be the Thunderbirds' starting goaltender. On March 6, Ellis signed a two-year, two-way contract extension worth $1.55 million with the Blues.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-41) Four days later, he was named AHL Player of the Week ending March 9 with a shutout, 95 saves, a 0.72 GAA, and a .979 save percentage.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-42) By the end of the season, he had played 42 games with a 22–14–5 record, a 2.63 GAA, and a .922 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) The Thunderbirds entered the [2025 Calder Cup playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Calder_Cup_playoffs "2025 Calder Cup playoffs") as the A6 seed paired against the A3 seed [Providence Bruins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence_Bruins "Providence Bruins"), a series they would lose in three; he recorded a 2.32 GAA and a .933 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2) Following the Calder Cup playoffs, Ellis was called up to the Blues on April 28, but did not appear in any Stanley Cup playoff games.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-43)

Before the start of the [2025–26 NHL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_NHL_season "2025–26 NHL season") on October 5, the Blues put Ellis on waivers to be put on assignment back to Springfield as [Jordan Binnington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Binnington "Jordan Binnington") and [Joel Hofer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Hofer "Joel Hofer") were expected to be the starter and backup, respectively.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-44) After impressive preseason play which caught the attention of [Buffalo Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Sabres "Buffalo Sabres") head coach [Lindy Ruff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindy_Ruff "Lindy Ruff"), he was claimed by the Sabres the next day, putting him and [Alexandar Georgiev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandar_Georgiev "Alexandar Georgiev") in contention for the backup spot to start the season behind [Alex Lyon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Lyon_/(ice_hockey/) "Alex Lyon (ice hockey)").[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-45) Georgiev was waived the following day, making Ellis the backup to Lyon to start the season.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-46) Ellis made his NHL debut on October 22 in a 4–2 win against the [Detroit Red Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Red_Wings "Detroit Red Wings"), saving 27 out of 29 shots on goal.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-47)[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-48) With his debut, he became the first goaltender from [Cape Breton Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Breton_Island "Cape Breton Island") to play in the NHL, the eighth from [Nova Scotia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Scotia "Nova Scotia"), and the ninth Sabres goaltender to win in their debut.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-49)

For the [2018 IIHF World U18 Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_IIHF_World_U18_Championships "2018 IIHF World U18 Championships"), Ellis and [Olivier Rodrigue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Rodrigue "Olivier Rodrigue") were selected as the team's goaltenders. He started the first two round-robin games against the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Hockey_National_Team_Development_Program "USA Hockey National Team Development Program") and [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus_men%27s_national_under-18_ice_hockey_team "Belarus men's national under-18 ice hockey team"), recording a 3.50 GAA and a .887 save percentage.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-EP-2)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-50) Rodrigue took over the starting goaltender role and Team Canada continued in quarterfinals play, where they lost to the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_men%27s_national_under-18_ice_hockey_team "Czech Republic men's national under-18 ice hockey team").[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-51)[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-52)

Ellis was contention for the [2020 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Junior_Ice_Hockey_Championships "2020 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships") roster for [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_men%27s_national_junior_ice_hockey_team "Canada men's national junior ice hockey team"), participating in what was considered an average summer showcase, but did not make the December camp roster cut.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-53)

On December 20, 2024, [Hockey Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockey_Canada "Hockey Canada") announced their roster for the [2024 Spengler Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Spengler_Cup "2024 Spengler Cup"), which selected Ellis and [Antoine Bibeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Bibeau "Antoine Bibeau") as the goaltenders. At the time of his selection, he had an 8–4–2 record with a 2.70 GAA and a .918 save percentage.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-54) He started the tournament in net against [HC Davos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HC_Davos "HC Davos"), recording 25 saves in a 6–2 win.[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TIO-55) Ellis continued to be the starting goaltender for Team Canada, playing two more games before losing to the [Straubing Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straubing_Tigers "Straubing Tigers") in the semifinals. He finished the tournament with a second-best 2.68 GAA and a .911 save percentage, only behind HC Davos goaltender [Luca Hollenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luca_Hollenstein "Luca Hollenstein").[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colten_Ellis#cite_note-TIO-55)

We're not far from the start of the regular season and, as such, teams are reducing their rosters to the required 23 players. The St. Louis Blues re-assigned defenseman Hunter Skinner to their AHL affiliate, the Springfield Thunderbirds, but another player is no longer a part of the organization.

Colton Ellis, a 25-year-old goaltender the Blues selected in the third round of the 2019 draft, was [claimed off waivers by the Buffalo Sabres](https://www.prohockeyrumors.com/2025/10/buffalo-sabres-claim-colten-ellis.html). Ellis had a decent career in the AHL, posting an average save percentage of .923 in 58 games across two seasons with the Thunderbirds. Due to his age and contract status, however, he was no longer waiver-exempt, allowing the Sabres to claim him off the waiver wire.

This shouldn't be too big of an impact for the Blues: at the NHL level, Jordan Binnington is the clear-cut starter, and Joel Hofer has the backup position locked up. In the AHL, the Blues also have goaltending prospects Vadim Zherenko and Will Cranely. Neither Zherenko nor Cranley has shown much yet to suggest they'll be NHL-quality goaltenders, but, in the short term, they should be good enough to backstop the Thunderbirds.

The Sabres, meanwhile, are struggling with their goaltending situation. Their presumptive starter, Ukko Pekka-Luukkonen, is going to miss time due to injury. Their backup situation isn't great, either: Devon Levi has potential, but needs more time to develop in the AHL; Alex Lyon is good when he can play, but injuries often keep him out of the crease; Alexander Georgiev's 2024-25, meanwhile, was the season from hell, and there's no telling whether he'll be able to rebound or not.

In any case, happy trail to Ellis--hopefully he finds more NHL success in Buffalo than he was ever likely to find in St. Louis.

7.content: MARYLAND HEIGHTS, Mo. -- Part of Doug Armstrong wanted to be selfish and keep goalie prospect Colten Ellis in the [St. Louis Blues](http://thn.com/stlouis) organization. But the Blues' GM also understands -- and is happy -- that the 25-year-old gets a crack to be on an NHL roster, something that may or may not have happened in St. Louis after Ellis was claimed off waivers by the [Buffalo Sabres](http://thn.com/buffalo) on Monday. The Blues are locked in with Jordan Binnington and Joel Hofer as their 1-2 punch in the NHL, and Ellis would have been the organization's No. 3 goalie on the depth chart and starter in Springfield of the American Hockey League, but the Blues needed waivers in order to put Ellis back in Springfield, and with the Sabres' starting goalie, Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, out week-to-week with a lower-body injury, and despite the Sabres having Alex Lyon, Alexandar Georgiev and Devin Levi available, Ellis is an intriguing option for Buffalo. Georgiev was put on waivers Tuesday and Levi was sent to their AHL affiliate in Rochester. Still, Armstrong was taken aback a bit to lose Ellis. "I'd say somewhat surprised," Armstrong said. "Only because he doesn't have that NHL resume. When he gets put into that first contest with the Sabres, it's his first contest (in the NHL). Sometimes when you're dealing with injuries, you're looking for stability of someone that's got a proven track record that the players can see. But he had a great year last year (22-14-2, 2.62 goals-against average, .922 save percentage). He's progressed very well. "When I called him yesterday, I said, 'I'm really happy for you and really disappointed for the organization because you've done everything you could to put yourself in a great spot.' He was clearly our No. 3 going into the year. Now he has the opportunity to take whatever Buffalo gives him and carve out an NHL career quickly. He wasn't going to get that obviously here with Hofer and Binnington." Blues coach Jim Montgomery echoed those thoughts. "It's a tough loss for our organization," Montgomery said. "A young man that ... he's a guy you cheer for. He started in the East Coast League, he just kept on working, kept on building his game and he's established himself as a premier goalie in the American League and had a really good camp. Every time he was in the nets, he's battling, he's making difficult saves look easy. So he's right on the cusp. It's unfortunate. We'll see how everything else develops from there from the goaltending aspect in our organization." Once the Sabres do get Luukkonen back, they could always carry three goalies, which isn't likely, but then they will have to put someone on waivers to assign them to Rochester, and if it's Ellis, the Blues could always reclaim him if given the chance and assign him right to Springfield. In the meantime, it does take away from Springfield's strengths, and the Thunderbirds would have gone with a tandem of Ellis and Vadim Zherenko, but now it will be Zherenko and Will Cranley for the foreseeable future. "Right now we'll go with 'Z' and Cranley," Armstrong said before joking. "It's a great business. The agents are always looking out for the St. Louis Blues. My phone is ringing off the hook on potential guys to help us. It's great to see everyone care about us." Making history in the crease: Buffalo Sabres’ Colten Ellis becomes first Cape Breton-born goaltender to play, earn a victory in the NHL
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last updated Oct 23, 2025

![Image 2: Colten Ellis of River Denys made 27 saves for record his first career NHL victory in his league debut against the Detroit Red Wings at KeyBank Center in Buffalo, N.Y., on Wednesday. Colten Ellis has etched his name into the Cape Breton sports record book with his first career NHL start on Wednesday night.

The River Denys product made 27 saves, backstopping the Buffalo Sabres to a 4-2 win over the Detroit Red Wings at KeyBank Center in Buffalo, N.Y.

Along with earning his first career victory, Ellis also made history becoming the first goaltender from Cape Breton to ever play in an NHL game.

Ellis is the eighth Nova Scotia-born goalie in NHL history and the ninth netminder in Sabres history to record a victory in his NHL debut.

“It’s huge for me, but it’s also huge for everybody in my family,” said Ellis in a post-game interview with the media.

“They’ve made so many sacrifices to help me get to this moment. And there’s so many supporters, too many to name. It’s been crazy, the support I’ve had since I was young, that played instrumental roles and helped me get to where I am.”

Ellis, who was claimed off waivers by the Sabres from St. Louis on Oct. 6, made several key saves in the contest, despite the Red Wings not recording their first shot on goal until the 10:16 mark of the first period.

Entering the game, the Red Wings had won five of their first six games and were sitting in the top six in the Eastern Conference standings with 10 points.

Jack Quinn had a goal and two assists while Jason Zucker, Josh Doan and Tyson Kozak netted goals for the Sabres (3-4-0-0).

J.T. Compher and Emmitt Finnie replied with goals for the Red Wings (5-2-0-0).

Detroit’s John Gibson turned aside 27 of 31 shots.

Ellis becomes the 27th Cape Bretoner to suit up for an NHL game behind Dave Amadio, Paul (Jigger) Andrea, Paul Boutilier, Nelson Burton, Tony Currie, Doug Doull, Trevor Fahey, Craig Ferguson, Norm Ferguson, John (Junior) Hanna, William (Flash) Hollett, Aaron Johnson, Andrew MacDonald, Parker MacDonald, Al MacInnis, Donald MacLean, Al MacNeil, Tommy McCarthy, Bill McDougall, Mike McPhee, Kevin Morrison, Daniel Poliziani, Logan Shaw, Bobby Smith, Sandy Snow and Doug Sulliman.

Alfie LeJeune of North Sydney refereed 725 career NHL games.

Ellis and the Sabres will return to the ice on Friday when they host the Toronto Maple Leafs at 8 p.m., Atlantic time, at KeyBank Center. The game will be broadcast live on Sportsnet One and TVA Sports.

Cape Breton’s Colten Ellis makes supporters proud after cracking Buffalo Sabres opening-night roster
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

‘He’s the definition of hard work and perseverance’

![Image 2: Colten Ellis of River Denys, left, will have an opportunity to prove himself as a member of the Buffalo Sabres. Ellis will be part of the NHL team's opening night roster on Thursday when the club hosts the New York Rangers. CONTRIBUTED/ LUCAS ARMSTRONG, SPRINGFIELD THUNDERBIRDS](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/cbp-26082024-colten-ellis-1-submitted_291905775.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&h=216&sig=_1Foh3mFgDw3_hGxmcrd4g)

Colten Ellis of River Denys, left, will have an opportunity to prove himself as a member of the Buffalo Sabres. Ellis will be part of the NHL team's opening night roster on Thursday when the club hosts the New York Rangers. Photo by Lucas Armstrong /Springfield Thunderbirds

It’s been a whirlwind week for Colten Ellis.

From being one of three goaltenders left at St. Louis Blues training camp to being placed on waivers by the team on Sunday and later [claimed by the Buffalo Sabres on Monday](https://www.saltwire.com/cape-breton/cape-bretons-colten-ellis-placed-on-waivers-by-st-louis-blues), it’s been a busy few days for the River Denys product.

While leaving the organization that drafted the 25-year-old in the third-round in 2019 surely wasn’t easy, Ellis will now have an opportunity to prove himself at the NHL level for the first time.

A day after being claimed off waivers, the Sabres announced that the six-foot-one, 185-pound Ellis will be part of the club’s opening night roster when they host the New York Rangers at KeyBank Center in Buffalo, N.Y.

To make room for Ellis, the Sabres placed goaltender Alexandar Georgiev on waivers on Tuesday, less than a month after the team signed the 29-year-old to a one-year deal worth $825,000 on Sept. 11.

![Image 3: Colten Ellis](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/cbp-26082024-colten-ellis-3-submitted_291905767-e1759927904665.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=nWyaOK66mwLG2wJGKsTEUQ)

Colten Ellis of River Denys was claimed off waivers by the Buffalo Sabres from the St. Louis Blues on Monday. Ellis will be among the team’s opening night roster on Thursday. Photo by Lucas Armstrong /Springfield Thunderbirds

‘HE PRIDES HIMSELF ON THE DETAILS’
----------------------------------

Ellis, who has never been on an NHL opening night roster in his career until now, will join Alex Lyon as the Buffalo’s goaltending tandem to start the season.

The 32-year-old Lyon has spent most of his career in the American Hockey League but has found a home in the NHL full-time the last three years. His best season in the league came in 2023-24 with the Detroit Red Wings, posting a 21-18-5 record along with a 3.05 goals-against average and a .905 save percentage in 44 games.

Last year, Lyon had a 14-9-1 record with a 2.81 goals-against average and a .896 save percentage in 30 games with the Red Wings. He signed a two-year, $3-million deal with the Sabres on July 1.

As for Ellis, since turning professional in 2021-22, he’s never played a game in the NHL to date, spending his pro career between the American Hockey League and the ECHL.

Now, with an opportunity in front of him, those who know Ellis well aren’t surprised with where he is in his career.

“I’m so happy and proud for Colten,” said Scott Gouthro, who serves as his goaltending coach during the summer.

“He’s the definition of hard work and perseverance. Every session of the summer, he prides himself on the details and habits that make him a pro. He has earned this chance. He’s not only a great goaltender, but an even better human being.”

Ellis acknowledged the chance provided to him by the Sabres in a media scrum with reporters on Tuesday.

This advertisement has not loaded yet.

This advertisement has not loaded yet, but your article continues below.

“It’s something I’ve worked for for 25 years now,” said Ellis. “Every day, just grinding to get better and work on what I can control. Just putting it all together and now having the opportunity to be in an NHL dressing room is awesome, and I’m super excited about it.”

Ellis, who originally signed a two-year contract extension with the Blues earlier this year, appeared in 42 games with the AHL’s Springfield Thunderbirds last season, posting a 22-14-3 record along with a 2.63 goals-against average and a .922 save percentage along with three shutouts.

Speaking with the media on Tuesday, Sabres head coach Lindy Ruff addressed Ellis joining the club.

“When Ellis became available, he’s someone that as an organization we felt really highly about,” said Ruff. “I like his puck play. I like how quick he is. (I) watched a good part of his games yesterday; (he has) a calmness about him. So, I can understand why he’s been on the radar.”

![Image 4: Colten Ellis](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/cbp-02052023-colten-ellis-j-fraser_291974367-e1759927960554.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=ygj4fjQbXvNxl23uUso8lg)

Colten Ellis of River Denys spent three years with the Rimouski Océanic after being traded to the Quebec-based team in June 2017. He later went on to finish his junior career with the Charlottetown Islanders. Photo by Jeremy Fraser /Cape Breton Post

LONG ROAD TO THE NHL
--------------------

Ellis began his career playing with the now former Whycocomagh Minor Hockey Association.

Later, he joined the Antigonish-based Nova Jr. X-Men of the Nova Scotia Under-15 Major Hockey League, playing with the club for two seasons from 2013 to 2015.

Following his time with the X-Men, Ellis suited up for the Cape Breton West Islanders of the Nova Scotia Under-18 Major Hockey League, backstopping the team to provincial and Atlantic championships and later a Telus Cup national title in 2017.

Brian MacInnis, president of the Cape Breton West Islanders, said nobody is shocked with how well Ellis is doing in his career.

“Everyone on this side of the island is extremely proud of Colten and everything he’s accomplished so far,” said MacInnis.

“His focus both on and off the ice was evident when he first joined the Islanders and of course his outstanding performance in Prince George, B.C., where he led the Islanders to the Telus Cup championship just proved he was headed in the right direction.

“Colten has always been extremely dedicated, has worked his hardest, and is a real role model for all young athletes in Cape Breton. Everyone is wishing him all the best in the upcoming season.”

![Image 5: Colten Ellis](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/aaamidgethockey7609_292477081.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&sig=yRPBMg4zixFhHw4Uz2l8-g)

Colten Ellis of the Cape Breton West Islanders, middle, makes a save during Nova Scotia Under-18 Major Hockey League action at the Dartmouth Sportsplex on March 24, 2017. Photo by File /Postmedia

In 2016, Ellis was drafted in the fourth-round, No. 59 overall, by the Cape Breton Eagles at the Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League Entry Draft. He played three games with the team in 2016-17 and had a 2-0-0-0 record.

[Ellis was later traded by the Eagles to the Rimouski Océanic](https://www.saltwire.com/atlantic-canada/six-years-later-former-cape-breton-eagles-head-coach-gm-discuss-decision-to-trade-colten-ellis-over-kevin-mandolese-100851095). He spent three seasons with the Quebec-based team from 2018 to 2020 before being traded to the Charlottetown Islanders.

In Charlottetown, Ellis guided the Islanders to a semifinal appearance in 2021. He was also given the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy for the league’s best goals-against average (1.78), becoming the first Cape Breton-born player to receive the honour. He also had the league’s best save percentage (.926) that season.

After junior, Ellis spent most of his first pro season with the Worcester Railers of the ECHL, posting a 15-13-5 record along with a 3.21 goals-against average and a .905 save percentage.

He also appeared in six games with the Thunderbirds, the affiliate of the Blues, posting a 1-3-3 record with a 3.93 goals-against-average and a .880 save percentage.

SIDELINED BY INJURY
-------------------

As the second season began with the ECHL’s Tulsa Oilers, Ellis intended to [prove himself and earn a spot back with the Thunderbirds](https://www.saltwire.com/atlantic-canada/cape-bretons-colten-ellis-named-echl-goaltender-of-the-week-100924309) until an unfortunate hip injury would halt his 2022-23 season.

Ellis would eventually have season-ending hip surgery in February 2023. He finished the season with a 12-9-5 record along with a 3.46 goals-against average and a .888 save percentage in 27 games.

After successful surgery, Ellis began the recovery process and got back on the ice training in June 2023. He continued to train throughout the summer and into September and [was ready for the start of Blues training camp](https://www.saltwire.com/atlantic-canada/cape-bretons-colten-ellis-given-opportunity-to-prove-himself-as-professional-goaltender-with-st-louis-blues-organization-100991072).

At camp, he had the opportunity to suit up for the team during the preseason in September 2023, but was later reassigned to the ECHL’s Orlando Solar Bears where he began the 2023-24 season, appearing in 21 games and posting a 12-5-1 record with a 2.45 goals-against average and a .923 save percentage.

As the calendar turned to January 2024, Ellis wouldn’t have much more time to soak up the sun in Florida when he was called up to Springfield on Jan. 21 for the remainder of the year.

In 16 games with the Thunderbirds, Ellis had a 7-9-0 record along with a 2.89 goals-against average and a .924 save percentage. He solidified his spot with the Thunderbirds in March 2024 when the Blues traded goaltender Malcolm Subban to the Columbus Blue Jackets, leading to his stellar 2024-25 campaign.

Ellis wasn’t the only goaltender placed on waivers in the NHL on Sunday. Michael DiPietro (Boston), Cayden Primeau (Carolina), Cal Petersen (Minnesota), Kaapo Kahkonen (Montreal) and Brandon Bussi (Florida) also hit the waiver wire.

As of publication time, the Sabres hadn’t announced their starter for the season opener on Thursday, however, it will likely be Lyon.

Puck drop for the Sabres and Rangers game is set for 8 p.m., Atlantic time. The game can be seen on Sportsnet+ and NHL Centre Ice in Canada as well as MSG and MSG-B in the United States.

BIO
---

### COLTEN ELLIS

Hometown: River Denys, N.S.

NHL Draft: Selected in the third-round, No. 93 overall, by the St. Louis Blues in 2019

CAREER STATISTICS
-----------------

2021-22 – Worcester (ECHL) – GP: 34 – Record: 15-13-5 – G.A.A.: 3.21 – SV%: .905

2021-22 – Springfield (AHL) – GP: 6 – Record: 1-3-3 – G.A.A.: 3.93 – SV%: .880

2023-24 – Springfield (AHL) – GP: 16 – Record: 7-9-0 – G.A.A.: 2.89 – SV%: .924

2024-25 – Springfield (AHL) – GP: 42 – Record: 22-14-5 – G.A.A.: 2.63 – SV%: .922

The [St. Louis Blues](https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/teams/st-louis-blues/line-combinations) [announced](https://www.nhl.com/blues/news/ellis-agrees-to-two-year-extension-with-blues) Thursday that the club has re-signed goaltender Colten Ellis to a two-year, two-way contract extension.

Through 31 appearances this season with the Springfield Thunderbirds, the Blues’ AHL affiliate, Ellis has posted a 19-7-3 record coupled with a .926 save percentage, 2.41 goals-against average, and two shutouts.

A 24-year-old native of Whycocomagh, N.S., Ellis is currently in his third season with the Thunderbirds. Last season, Ellis saw 16 showings with the Thunderbirds in which he went 7-9-0 with a .924 save percentage and 2.89 goals-against average. Ellis also split time last season with the ECHL’s Orlando Solar Bears counting 21 appearances in which he went 12-5-2 with a .923 save percentage, 2.45 goals-against average, and one shutout.

In all, Ellis has totaled a 27-19-8 record through 53 total games over three AHL seasons as well as a 39-27-11 showing in 82 games over three seasons at the ECHL level.

Ellis was originally chosen 93rd overall by the Blues in the 2019 NHL Draft.

A graduate of the QMJHL’s Charlottetown Islanders, Ellis’ final junior season in 2020-21 saw him named to the league’s First All-Star Team after he led all goaltenders with a .926 save percentage and 1.78 goals-against average. Ellis’ accolades in the junior circuit also included All-Rookie Team recognition in 2017-18 when as part of the Rimouski Oceanic he impressed with a 33-8-1 record alongside a .913 save percentage, 2.35 goals-against average, and six shutouts.

With the signing, Ellis becomes one of two goaltenders under contract with the Blues next season. Entering the 2025-26 season, 31-year-old starter Jordan Binnington has two years remaining on his contract at a $6-million annual average value, according to [PuckPedia](https://puckpedia.com/player/jordan-binnington). Additionally, current backup Joel Hofer is [eligible to become a restricted free agent](https://puckpedia.com/player/joel-hofer) at the conclusion of the 2024-25 campaign.

BUFFALO, N.Y. (AP) — Jack Quinn had a goal and two assists, Colten Ellis stopped 27 shots in his NHL debut and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Detroit Red Wings 4-2 on Wednesday night.

Claimed off waivers from St. Lous earlier this month, Ellis stopped two breakaways and withstood a flurry of shots after Detroit pulled goalie John Gibson with about three minutes left.

Buffalo’s Tyson Kozak scored for the second straight game and Jason Zucker had a goal before leaving in the second period with an upper-body injury. Josh Doan also scored for the Sabres.

J.T. Compher and Emmitt Finnie scored for Detroit, which had won five straight. Gibson had 27 saves and Dylan Larkin had an assist to become the first Detroit defenseman with a season-opening points streak of seven games since Brian Rafalski in 2008-09.

Ellis became the eighth Nova Scotia-born goalie in NHL history and the ninth goalie in Sabres history to win his NHL debut. The 25-year-old didn’t face a shot in the opening 10 minutes, but stopped Marco Kasper on a breakaway late in the first period.

Ellis stopped Larkin on another breakaway early in the second period before Compher beat him on a nifty move, corralling a pass from Albert Johansson and whipping it to his forehand.
